title: Migrate FastAPI monolith request bodies from raw dict to Pydantic BaseModel schemas
description: Brownfield Python migration: replace raw dict parameters with typed Pydantic BaseModel request/response schemas in the FastAPI monolith. All existing tests must pass.

task_spec.prompt:
Migrate src/app.py to use Pydantic BaseModel request schemas (fastapi already depends on pydantic — no new deps needed).

Add these models (in src/app.py or a new src/schemas.py):
  class UserCreate(BaseModel): username: str; email: str = ""
  class PostCreate(BaseModel): title: str; body: str = ""; author_id: int | None = None
  class CommentCreate(BaseModel): text: str

Update endpoint signatures:
  create_user(body: UserCreate) — keep manual 'if not body.username: HTTPException(400)'
  create_post(body: PostCreate) — keep manual 'if not body.title: HTTPException(400)'
  create_comment(post_id: int, body: CommentCreate) — keep manual 'if not body.text: HTTPException(400)'

Response shapes and status codes must not change.
All 7 existing tests must still pass.
Run: uv run pytest tests/ -v
required_artifacts: UserCreate BaseModel with username and email fields
PostCreate BaseModel with title, body, author_id fields
create_user accepts UserCreate, validates username non-empty
create_post accepts PostCreate, validates title non-empty
success_criteria: uv run ruff check src/ passes
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` to verify the migration is correct. Make sure existing behavior is preserved and the migration handles edge cases safely.
Final verification: run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` and confirm all tests pass. Is this migration safe to run on real data without data loss or breaking existing clients?
